newsitem.title: POLAND: Investment risk in Polish economy falls - study.
newsitem.headline: Investment risk in Polish economy falls - study.

text.p: The risk of investing in Polish companies is falling thanks to the progress in the country's economic transition and bullish economic climate, a study by independent Gdansk Institute for Market Economy (IBnGR) said.

"Investment risk in all sectors of the Polish economy is falling gradually which means Poland is becoming increasingly attractive," Janusz Dabrowski, the institute's deputy director , told a news conference.
"Entire industries are becoming less sensitive to foreign competition," he added, presenting the institute's semi-annual study for the first half of 1996.

The study asseses the total investment risk linked to the quality of management and efficiency of companies, their position within a given branch and factors independent from the companies such as government regulations.
Bohdan Wyznikiewicz, who oversaw the project, said the number of industries with high investment risk has fallen while the group of low-risk segments was expanding.
"The number of branches with the very high investment risk has significantly fallen," Wyznikiewicz said.
He said manufacturing of building materials and food processing were among the least risky industries along with specialised merchandising. Also niche players ranked in the lowest-risk class.
"The least risky are small branches...which are not technologically advanced but fill market niches," Wyznikiewicz said.
The IBnGR's "investment risk map" compiled for Bank Rozwoju Eksportu SA (BRE) covers 179 industrial segments and 105 non-manufacturing sectors.
